title: Detached tool invocation semantics and schema anchoring — acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines acceptance criteria for a new pattern we call 'detached tool invocation' and the associated schema anchoring model. Detached invocations are cases where the model emits a tool call token sequence that may be validated and executed later (out-of-band or after partial stream emission). Schema anchoring ensures every partial or detached emission is associated with a minimal, verifiable schema stub enabling safe reconciliation and retries.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic rules for how emitted structured fragments map to canonical schemas when the full object is not yet available (streaming & detached flows).
- Define failure modes and expected server/client behaviors for validation errors, truncated streams, and idempotent replays for detached tool calls.
- Specify telemetry and QA checks to measure correctness and regression.

Scope (in-scope):
- API-level acceptance criteria for streaming structured output with detached tool calls (hosted + dedicated).
- Schema anchoring format (schema_id + fragment_path + partial_hash).
- Server-side validation strategies and canonical error envelopes for clients to consume.
- Rollout plan with canary and feature-flag controls.

Out of scope:
- Full runtime kernel-level batching changes to support new backpressure signals (separate ENG ticket).
- SDK ergonomics beyond minimal helper functions for parsing anchored fragments.

Acceptance criteria (must all pass for this ticket to be marked Done):
1) Schema anchoring envelope: Every detached or partial structured emission MUST include an anchoring envelope with three fields: schema_id (string), fragment_path (JSONPath-style string), and fragment_hash (hex string). Example: {"schema_id":"redwood.v2.chatAction","fragment_path":"$.actions[0]","fragment_hash":"a3f5..."}. The envelope may be sent as the first token of a structured chunk or as a metadata frame.

2) Deterministic merge rules: Given a set of anchored fragments for the same schema_id and root_id, the server MUST be able to deterministically merge fragments by applying fragments in increasing fragment_path order and treating later fields as authoritative when paths conflict. Tests must include nested-object conflict scenarios and array-indexed fragments.

3) Partial validation levels: The platform must support three validation levels per request: permissive, strict, and audit. Acceptance tests must cover each level:
  - permissive: accept fragments with unknown fields and emit a validation warning metric
  - strict: reject fragments that contain unknown or type-mismatched fields with canonical error code INVALID_FRAGMENT
  - audit: accept but record full diff against canonical schema for later analysis

4) Detached tool-call idempotency: Detached tool calls include a client-provided invocation_id. The system must guarantee at-least-once execution semantics by default and provide an idempotency window (configurable; default 5 minutes). Replays within the window must not produce duplicate external side effects. Acceptance tests will simulate duplicate invocation messages and verify no double-execution on a mock tool backend.

5) Stream truncation & reconciliation: If a streaming response ends with an unresolved anchored fragment (missing required child fields), the response must include an explicit terminal state frame: {"anchoring_status":"incomplete","schema_id":...,"missing_paths":[...]}. Clients must treat this as a recoverable partial state and be able to fetch the remaining fragments via a /fragments/fetch endpoint (API contract documented in linked PRD).

6) Canonical error envelope: All validation or tool-execution errors MUST be returned as a structured error envelope with fields: error_code, human_message, related_schema_id (optional), related_fragment_hash (optional), retryable (boolean). Error_codes are from the canonical list: INVALID_FRAGMENT, TOOL_EXEC_FAILURE, STREAM_TRUNCATED, UNAUTHORIZED, INTERNAL. Acceptance tests intentionally trigger each code and assert envelope conformance.

7) Backpressure hint header for SDKs: When server detects slow downstream tool execution queues that would breach token-latency SLOs, it should emit a backpressure hint header in the streaming session: X-RW-Backpressure: level=medium;estimated_delay_ms=320. SDK tests must surface this header and expose a callback for clients to stall or degrade fidelity.

8) Observability & metrics: For every anchored emission record the following telemetry: anchor.emitted (counter), anchor.validated (counter + validation_level tag), anchor.validation_error (counter + error_code), anchor.merged_latency_ms (histogram), tool.invocations.detached (counter), tool.invocation.duplicate_detected (counter). Dashboards must exist in the 'Structured Output' board. QA will validate that metrics appear during e2e tests.

9) Test harness and artifacts: Provide a test harness with a mock tool backend that supports idempotency tokens and a fragment fetch endpoint. Include unit tests (server validation), integration tests (stream + fetch reconciliation), and an end-to-end smoke test that runs on a canary fleet. Link to test spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Detached+Tool+Invocations (placeholder).

10) Rollout & rollback criteria: Start with 2% traffic canary on runtime-1.22 for 72h. If anchor.validation_error rate > 0.3% or tool.invocation.duplicate_detected > 0.05% in the first 72h, rollback automatically. Manual rollback criteria: customer_error_reports > 2 for customers with canary flag.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We choose anchored fragments over inline coercion to avoid repeated full-object emission for long-running generators; this reduces token cost but requires merge semantics.
- Strict validation is opt-in per-request to avoid breaking existing customers; default will be permissive for the first release.
- Detached idempotency relies on invocation_id namespace; SDKs must ensure globally unique ids for cross-region durability.

Linkage to artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/structured-output-detached (placeholder)
- Draft API spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/2486 (placeholder)

2025-10-31: ENG comment (N. Patel) — suggested using JSON Pointer paths instead of JSONPath for deterministic ordering. Accepted; updated merge rules to 'JSONPath-style' but real impl will use JSON Pointer.
2025-11-01: Design review (A. Kumar) — requested explicit terminal state frame for truncated streams; added acceptance criterion #5.
2025-11-03: QA added test plan skeleton and linked mock tool harness repo. Assigned Rafael to coordinate integration tests.
notes: QA owners: Priya Singh. Dev lead: Nikhil Patel. Security reviewed: basic design reviewed; no secrets in anchor envelopes. See linked security checklist in Confluence.
acceptance_tests: Provided in test harness. Tests include: merge_conflict_nested_objects, idempotent_replay_no_double_execution, truncated_stream_terminal_frame, validation_levels_permissive_strict_audit, backpressure_header_received, metrics_emitted_verification.
